proof:
Source: Step 1 and condition (G3) of Step 2 of the parent proof. This is the documented correction to the printed Proof of 8.2: the rescaled masses of T_{j′} stay bounded because x is chosen with Θ*ⁿ(ν, x) < ∞ for a weak limit ν of the mass measures. That is what justifies the printed "(8) remains valid with T_{j′} instead of T". Steps 1–5 below supply the details.

Conventions.
- ℝ^P := Eucl P, Hⁿ := μHE[n] on ℝ^P, and B_r(x), B̄_r(x) are the open and closed balls.
- K_R := B̄_R(0) for R ∈ ℕ.
- M_W(X) := X.massOn W and M(X) := X.mass = M_{ℝ^P}(X).
- For a finite Borel measure ν on ℝ^P, Θ*ⁿ(ν, x) := dimensionalUpperDensity ν.toOuterMeasure n univ x = limsup_{r↓0} ν(B̄_r(x))/(ω_n rⁿ), where ω_n := realUnitBallVolume n = π^{n/2}/Γ(n/2 + 1) ∈ (0, ∞).
- Λ := sup_j M(T_j) < ∞.

1. Mass measures. Fix j. Every open W with compact closure satisfies M_W(T_j) ≤ M(T_j) ≤ Λ < ∞, by monotonicity of massOn in W (GeometricCurrentOn.massOn_mono). Part (R2) of the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.iwl_restriction_theory, with U := ℝ^P, then gives a Borel measure μ_j on ℝ^P with IsMassMeasure T_j μ_j, i.e. μ_j(W) = M_W(T_j) for every open W ⊂⊂ ℝ^P (every open W with compact closure). The accepted Submission.rectifiability_mass_measure_representation would serve equally. Two consequences:
 (1a) μ_j(B_r(x)) = M_{B_r(x)}(T_j) for all x ∈ ℝ^P and r ∈ ℝ. For r ≤ 0 both sides vanish, since B_r(x) = ∅ and M_∅ = 0.
 (1b) μ_j(ℝ^P) = sup_{R∈ℕ} μ_j(B_R(0)) = sup_R M_{B_R(0)}(T_j) ≤ Λ, by continuity from below along the increasing union ⋃_R B_R(0) = ℝ^P.
 So each μ_j is a finite Borel measure of total mass ≤ Λ.

2. Weak compactness on the balls K_R (Simon Ch. 1, 4.16).
 (2a) Compactness for one R. Let μ_j^R := μ_j⌞K_R, a finite Borel measure with μ_j^R(ℝ^P) ≤ Λ that vanishes off K_R. Every sequence (μ^R_{a(i)})_i has a subsequence converging weakly (narrowly, as finite measures on ℝ^P) to a finite Borel measure vanishing off K_R. Proof:
  - The subtype K_R is a nonempty compact metrizable space (isCompact_closedBall; 0 ∈ K_R).
  - Apply SimonGMT Chapter01 finiteMeasure_tendsto_subseq_of_compact_metrizable (the compact-domain version of Simon 4.16; see also simon_theorem_4_16_compact_metrizable) to the finite measures μ_{a(i)}.comap Subtype.val on K_R, whose masses are ≤ Λ.toNNReal. This gives a subsequence converging weakly to some finite measure ν̃ on K_R.
  - Push forward along the continuous map Subtype.val. FiniteMeasure.map is continuous for the weak topology, and (μ.comap val).map val = μ⌞K_R because K_R is closed, hence measurable.
  - So the corresponding subsequence of μ^R_{a(i)} converges weakly to ν := ν̃.map val, which vanishes off K_R.
  (Mathlib's MeasureTheory.isCompact_setOfPred_finiteMeasure_le_of_isCompact gives the same compactness, but Mathlib proves metrizability of the weak topology only for probability measures. Hence the SimonGMT route, which normalizes masses, is the primary one.)
 (2b) Nested subsequences. Apply (2a) for R = 0, 1, 2, …, each time to the subsequence produced at the previous stage. This gives strictly increasing maps χ_0, χ_1, … and finite Borel measures ν_R (vanishing off K_R, with ν_R(ℝ^P) ≤ Λ by weak convergence of total masses) such that μ^R_{χ_0∘⋯∘χ_R(i)} → ν_R weakly as i → ∞.
 (2c) Diagonal. Put φ(j) := (χ_0∘⋯∘χ_j)(j).
  - φ is strictly increasing: χ_{j+1}(j+1) ≥ j+1 > j and χ_0∘⋯∘χ_j is strictly increasing, so φ(j+1) = (χ_0∘⋯∘χ_j)(χ_{j+1}(j+1)) > (χ_0∘⋯∘χ_j)(j) = φ(j).
  - Fix R. For j ≥ R, φ(j) = (χ_0∘⋯∘χ_R)(ρ_R(j)), where ρ_R(R) := R and ρ_R(j) := (χ_{R+1}∘⋯∘χ_j)(j) for j > R. The map ρ_R is strictly increasing on {j ≥ R}, by the same argument.
  - Hence (μ^R_{φ(j)})_{j≥R} is a subsequence of (μ^R_{χ_0∘⋯∘χ_R(i)})_i, and μ^R_{φ(j)} → ν_R weakly as j → ∞, for every R ∈ ℕ.

3. Portmanteau. For every R ∈ ℕ and every closed F ⊆ ℝ^P, limsup_{j→∞} μ^R_{φ(j)}(F) ≤ ν_R(F) (Mathlib MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.limsup_measure_closed_le_of_tendsto).

4. Comparison (Simon Ch. 1, 3.3). Fix R and let A_R := {x ∈ ℝ^P : Θ*ⁿ(ν_R, x) = ∞}. For every t ∈ ℕ, t ≤ Θ*ⁿ(ν_R, x) for all x ∈ A_R. Apply the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.rectifiability_density_comparison, whose statement is
  ∀ P n ν A V t, IsOpen V → A ⊆ V → (∀ x ∈ A, t ≤ dimensionalUpperDensity ν.toOuterMeasure n univ x) → t·Hⁿ(A) ≤ ν(V),
 with ν := ν_R, A := A_R and V := ℝ^P. It gives t·Hⁿ(A_R) ≤ ν_R(ℝ^P) ≤ Λ < ∞. Since t ∈ ℕ is arbitrary, Hⁿ(A_R) = 0. Hence A := ⋃_{R∈ℕ} A_R satisfies Hⁿ(A) = 0.

5. Conclusion. Let x ∈ ℝ^P ∖ A and fix R ∈ ℕ with R ≥ ‖x‖ + 1. Then Θ := Θ*ⁿ(ν_R, x) < ∞.
 (5a) Since limsup_{r↓0} ν_R(B̄_r(x))/(ω_n rⁿ) = Θ < Θ + 1 (in [0, ∞]), there is r₁ > 0 with ν_R(B̄_r(x))/(ω_n rⁿ) < Θ + 1 for all r ∈ (0, r₁). Since ω_n rⁿ ∈ (0, ∞), this means ν_R(B̄_r(x)) < (Θ + 1)ω_n rⁿ.
 (5b) Put r₀ := min(r₁, 1) > 0 and C := 2(Θ + 1)ω_n, a real number in (0, ∞).
 (5c) Let r ∈ (0, r₀). The closed ball B̄_r(x) lies in K_R, because ‖y‖ ≤ ‖x‖ + r < R. Hence μ^R_{φ(j)}(B̄_r(x)) = μ_{φ(j)}(B̄_r(x)), and by step 3
  limsup_j μ_{φ(j)}(B̄_r(x)) ≤ ν_R(B̄_r(x)) < (Θ + 1)ω_n rⁿ < C rⁿ,
 the last inequality because (Θ + 1)ω_n rⁿ > 0.
 (5d) Therefore μ_{φ(j)}(B̄_r(x)) < C rⁿ for all sufficiently large j. For those j, by (1a),
  M_{B_r(x)}(T_{φ(j)}) = μ_{φ(j)}(B_r(x)) ≤ μ_{φ(j)}(B̄_r(x)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(C rⁿ).
 (5e) Since Hⁿ(A) = 0, this holds for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ ℝ^P, with the strictly increasing φ of step 2. That is the claim. ∎

Accepted declarations used (reuse by name, identical frozen type, to make them available to this node's Lean proof): Submission.iwl_restriction_theory, Submission.rectifiability_density_comparison.
key_steps: Mass measures μ_j of T_j from iwl_restriction_theory (R2): μ_j(B_r(x)) = M_{B_r(x)}(T_j) and μ_j(ℝ^P) ≤ Λ.
Weak compactness of μ_j⌞B̄_R(0) on each compact ball (SimonGMT compact-metrizable 4.16), and a diagonal subsequence φ with μ_{φ(j)}⌞B̄_R(0) → ν_R weakly for every R.
Portmanteau: limsup_j μ_{φ(j)}(F) ≤ ν_R(F) for closed F ⊆ B̄_R(0).
Off these null sets, Θ*ⁿ(ν_R,x) < ∞ gives ν_R(B̄_r(x)) < (Θ+1)ω_n rⁿ for small r, hence eventually M_{B_r(x)}(T_{φ(j)}) ≤ C rⁿ.
